e-3789.knowledge_point: Solving a Trigonometric Equation Containing the Tangent Function Transformed by Multiple Operations
e-3789.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3})-2 & =0 \\ 2\sqrt{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3}) & =2 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3}) & =\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{3} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(6n-1)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0, \pm 1, \pm 2,\ldots$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0 \leq x \lt 2\pi.$ Notice that setting $n=0$ gives a result outside of the domain.

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\dfrac{5\pi}{12}.$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\dfrac{11\pi}{12}.$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\dfrac{17\pi}{12}.$

- Setting $n=4$ gives $x=\dfrac{23\pi}{12}.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0 \leq x \lt 2\pi.$ So, the solutions $x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x = \dfrac{5\pi}{12}, \dfrac{11\pi}{12}, \dfrac{17\pi}{12}, \dfrac{23\pi}{12} .
$$

e-3794.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+\frac{\pi }{4} & =\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =-\frac{\pi }{4}+\frac{\pi }{4}+n\pi  \\ 3x & =n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{n\pi }{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0, \pm 1, \pm 2,\ldots,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-\pi < x \leq \pi.$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=0.$

- Setting $n=\pm1$ gives $x=\pm\dfrac{\pi}{3}.$

- Setting $n=\pm2$ gives $x=\pm\dfrac{2\pi}{3}.$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\pi.$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-\pi < x \leq \pi.$ So, the solutions are

$$
x = 0,\, \pm \dfrac{\pi}{3},\, \pm\dfrac{2\pi}{3}, \, \pi.
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{7\pi }{3} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{7\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =-\frac{13\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{13\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(6n-13)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=4$ gives $x=\frac{11\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=5$ gives $x=\frac{17\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=6$ gives $x=\frac{23\pi }{12}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{5\pi }{12},\,\frac{11\pi }{12},\,\frac{17\pi }{12},\,\frac{23\pi }{12}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{1}=\frac{5\pi }{12}$ and ${x}_{4}=\frac{23\pi }{12},$ we have

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{4}=\frac{5\pi }{12}+\frac{23\pi }{12}=\frac{28\pi }{12}=\frac{7\pi }{3}.
$$

Question 6
?

Consider the equation tan⁡(2x+7π3)=33 for 0≤x<2π. If the exact solutions x1,x2,x3 and x4 are written in ascending order, what is the value of x1+x4?

a
11π6
b
13π12
c
7π6
d
11π3
e
7π3
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

2x+7π3=π6+nπ.

Solving the equation above for x, we get

2x=−7π3+π6+nπ2x=−13π6+nπx=−13π12+nπ2x=(6n−13)π12.

We set n=0,±1,±2,…, until we have generated all solutions in the domain 0≤x<2π.

  • Setting n=3 gives x=5π12

  • Setting n=4 gives x=11π12

  • Setting n=5 gives x=17π12

  • Setting n=6 gives x=23π12

All other values of n generate solutions outside the domain 0≤x<2π. So, the solutions x1,x2,x3,x4 (written in ascending order) are

x=5π12,11π12,17π12,23π12.

Finally, since x1=5π12 and x4=23π12, we have

x1+x4=5π12+23π12=28π12=7π3.

content.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{7\pi }{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{4}?$
content.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{7\pi }{3} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{7\pi }{3}+\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =-\frac{13\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{13\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(6n-13)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=4$ gives $x=\frac{11\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=5$ gives $x=\frac{17\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=6$ gives $x=\frac{23\pi }{12}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{5\pi }{12},\,\frac{11\pi }{12},\,\frac{17\pi }{12},\,\frac{23\pi }{12}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{1}=\frac{5\pi }{12}$ and ${x}_{4}=\frac{23\pi }{12},$ we have

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{4}=\frac{5\pi }{12}+\frac{23\pi }{12}=\frac{28\pi }{12}=\frac{7\pi }{3}.
$$

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{2})+\sqrt{3}=0$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{4}?$
after.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{2})+\sqrt{3} & =0 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{\pi }{2} & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(1+6n)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{7\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{13\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{19\pi }{12}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{12},\frac{7\pi }{12},\frac{13\pi }{12},\frac{19\pi }{12}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{12}$ and ${x}_{4}=\frac{19\pi }{12},$ we have

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{4}=\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{19\pi }{12}=\frac{20\pi }{12}=\frac{5\pi }{3}.
$$

The general solution to our equation is

2x−π2=−π3+nπ.

Solving the equation above for x, we get

2x=π2−π3+nπ2x=π6+nπx=π12+nπ2x=(1+6n)π12.

All other values of n generate solutions outside the domain 0≤x<2π. So, the solutions x1,x2,x3,x4 (written in ascending order) are

content.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{2})+\sqrt{3}=0$ for $0\le x<2\pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{4}?$
content.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{2})+\sqrt{3} & =0 \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡(2x-\frac{\pi }{2}) & =-\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-\frac{\pi }{2} & =-\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{\pi }{2}-\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(1+6n)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{7\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{13\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=3$ gives $x=\frac{19\pi }{12}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<2\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{12},\frac{7\pi }{12},\frac{13\pi }{12},\frac{19\pi }{12}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{1}=\frac{\pi }{12}$ and ${x}_{4}=\frac{19\pi }{12},$ we have

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{4}=\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{19\pi }{12}=\frac{20\pi }{12}=\frac{5\pi }{3}.
$$

Consider the equation tan⁡(2x+π3)=33 for −π<x≤π. If the exact solutions x1,x2,x3 and x4 are written in ascending order, what is the value of x2+x3?

a
5π12
b
π6
c
π4
d
π3
e
π2
Submit

decision.explanation: Since tan(π/6)=√3/3, 2x+π/3=π/6+nπ, giving x=−π/12+nπ/2. In −π<x≤π, the ascending solutions are −7π/12, −π/12, 5π/12, and 11π/12. Thus x₂+x₃=4π/12=π/3.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡(2x+\frac{\pi }{3})=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $-\pi <x\le \pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ and ${x}_{4}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{2}+{x}_{3}?$
after.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x+\frac{\pi }{3} & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =\frac{\pi }{6}-\frac{\pi }{3}+n\pi  \\ 2x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(6n-1)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $-\pi <x\le \pi .$

- Setting $n=-1$ gives $x=-\frac{7\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=-\frac{\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{11\pi }{12}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $-\pi <x\le \pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3},{x}_{4}$ (written in ascending order) are

$$
x=-\frac{7\pi }{12},\,-\frac{\pi }{12},\,\frac{5\pi }{12},\,\frac{11\pi }{12}.
$$

Finally, since ${x}_{2}=-\frac{\pi }{12}$ and ${x}_{3}=\frac{5\pi }{12},$ we have

$$
{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=-\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{5\pi }{12}=\frac{\pi }{3}.
$$

x=−7π12,−π12,5π12,11π12.

Finally, since x2=−π12 and x3=5π12, we have

x2+x3=−π12+5π12=π3.

decision.explanation: Since tan(−π/6)=−√3/3, 2x=−π/6+nπ, so x=−π/12+nπ/2. The solutions in 0≤x<π are 5π/12 and 11π/12. Their sum is 16π/12=4π/3.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the exact solutions to the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡2x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $0\le x<\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{2}?$
after.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the equation above for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{\pi }{12}+\frac{n\pi }{2} \\ x & =\frac{(6n-1)\pi }{12}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<\pi .$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{5\pi }{12}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{11\pi }{12}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<\pi .$ So, the solutions are $x=\frac{5\pi }{12},\frac{11\pi }{12}.$

Finally, 

$$
{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{12}+\frac{11\pi }{12}=\frac{4\pi }{3}.
$$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: Consider the equation $\operatorname{tan}⁡3x=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}$ for $0\le x<\pi .$ If the exact solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2}$ and ${x}_{3}$ are written in ascending order, what is the value of ${x}_{1}+{x}_{3}?$
after.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}3x & =\frac{\pi }{6}+n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving our equation for $x,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =\frac{\pi }{18}+\frac{n\pi }{3} \\ x & =\frac{(1+6n)\pi }{18}.\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=\frac{\pi }{18}$

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{7\pi }{18}$

- Setting $n=2$ gives $x=\frac{13\pi }{18}$

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<\pi .$ So, the solutions ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},{x}_{3}$ (written in ascending order) are 

$$
x=\frac{\pi }{18},\frac{7\pi }{18},\frac{13\pi }{18}.
$$

Finally, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+{x}_{3} & =\frac{\pi }{18}+\frac{13\pi }{18} \\  & =\frac{14\pi }{18} \\  & =\frac{7\pi }{9}.\end{aligned}
$$
